newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Violence declines during Brazil's Rio carnival.
newsitem.headline: Violence declines during Brazil's Rio carnival.

text.p: Violent crime over the four days of this year's world famous carnival celebrations declined from a year ago, state public security officials said Thursday.
Police recorded 41 murders in the city between Saturday and Tuesday, down from 44 last year.

"The homicide figures were no higher than on normal days, despite the huge crowds of people in public places drinking alcohol and celebrating carnival," said State Public Security Secretary Nilton Cerqueira.

Tourists also remained largely unharmed during the festivities, with 39 thefts and robberies committed against visitors, Cerqueira said. There were no incidents involving tourists at the sambadrome stadium where the colourful samba school parades are held.

This year's carnival, which was also seen as a test for Rio's bid to hold the 2004 Olympic Games, attracted some 300,000 tourists, 15 percent more than last year, according to the Association of Brazilian Travel Agents.
Hotels were fully booked and the celebrations represented a turnover of $1 billion in alcohol sales, restaurant bills and hotel reservations.
